federation.title: Multi-device library
federation.intro: Browse the libraries on your devices together. Each device keeps its own resources; this view is read-only.
federation.cancelled: Query cancelled. Search again to create a new result session.
federation.name.label: Device name
federation.name.tip: Other devices see this name. Up to 64 characters.
federation.localOnly: Open Bakabase on the device whose libraries you want to browse. Multi-device is managed from each device's own window.
federation.scope.label: Search scope
federation.search.label: Name search
federation.search.placeholder: Match a resource name or file name
federation.search.tip: Matches names and file names across the selected devices. Use the local library for advanced property filters. Refreshing starts a new snapshot; devices that reconnect are not silently added to existing results.
federation.availability.label: Files
federation.sort.label: Order
federation.results.partialTip: Devices missing from the coverage were not searched, so their resources are not included in these results. This does not mean they have none. Search again to retry them with a new snapshot.
federation.expired: This result session has expired. The displayed results are kept, but more pages need a new search.
federation.empty.title: No matching resources
federation.empty.partial: No matches on the responding devices
federation.empty.tip: Try a different name, or add a device to browse. An empty local library doesn't stop you browsing other devices.
federation.detail.title: Resource details
federation.detail.readOnly: These values were resolved by the source device. No metadata or playback history is written back from this view.
federation.detail.mediaTip: Playback runs on this device. Linking a file does not guarantee that the source can still read it.
federation.detail.noMedia: No supported media is available for this resource.
federation.devices.title: Devices and sharing
federation.devices.intro: Manage your other Bakabase devices, or share libraries with them. Managing gives full control; library sharing only lets a device browse, never change anything.
federation.devices.nav.label: Sections of Devices and sharing
federation.devices.nav.pendingManage: , {{count}} requests to manage waiting for you
federation.devices.nav.pendingShare: , {{count}} requests to browse waiting for you
federation.devices.tabIntro.manage: Managing is full control: open another device's Bakabase in this window and change settings, organise files and run tasks, as if you sat in front of it. Playing files and opening folders still happen on this device. Management and library sharing are independent and use different codes.
federation.devices.tabIntro.sharing: Library sharing lets devices browse each other's libraries — search, view and play, never change. Each direction is allowed on its own: browsing a device doesn't let it browse you.
federation.devices.addresses.title: Addresses other devices use to reach {{target}}
federation.devices.addresses.virtual: Virtual adapter — other devices usually can't reach it
federation.devices.addresses.linkLocal: No network address assigned — other devices can't reach it
federation.devices.addresses.tip: Enter the recommended address on the other device; if it's on another network, pick one it can reach.
federation.devices.addresses.remoteOff: Remote access is off, so no other device can reach {{target}} right now.
federation.devices.addresses.none: No local network address was found for {{target}}, so other devices can't reach it yet. Check the network, then refresh.
federation.devices.openManagementAccess: Go to Who may manage this device
federation.devices.waiting.title: Waiting for you
federation.devices.waiting.browse: {{name}} asks to browse this device's library
federation.devices.waiting.unrestricted: Any device on the network has full control of this device
federation.devices.chooser.title: Add another device
federation.devices.chooser.manage.title: Manage it from this device
federation.devices.chooser.manage.desc: Full control — settings, files and tasks, as if you sat in front of it. Needs a pairing code from it, or its approval.
federation.devices.chooser.browse.title: Browse its library from this device
federation.devices.chooser.browse.desc: Read-only — search, view and play, never change. Needs a share code from it, or its approval.
federation.devices.status.title: Status
federation.devices.id.title: Device ID
federation.devices.id.tip: Other devices recognise this device by it; you may need it when troubleshooting. If the data folder is copied to another computer, both computers have the same ID — see below.
federation.devices.nav.pendingShare_one: , {{count}} request to browse waiting for you
federation.devices.nav.pendingManage_one: , {{count}} request to manage waiting for you
federation.devices.empty: This device can't browse any device yet. Add one below.
federation.devices.inboundEmpty: No device can browse this one yet.
federation.devices.include: Show its resources in the Multi-device library
federation.devices.forgetConfirm: Stop browsing {{name}}'s library? Nothing on {{name}} is deleted, and whether it can browse this device doesn't change.
federation.devices.revokeConfirm: Revoke {{name}}'s access to this device's library? Its searches and playback stop at once; what it has already seen can't be taken back.
federation.devices.removeConfirm: Remove {{name}}? Neither device can browse the other any more, and this device deletes its path mappings and pending requests. Add it again to undo this. What it has already seen can't be taken back.
federation.sharing.description: When on, devices you allow can browse this device's library — search, view and play — but can't change or delete anything. No device is allowed automatically.
federation.sharing.title: Share this device's library
federation.sharing.unpaired: Note: this device's remote access lets unpaired devices open it in a browser to view and play, whatever this sharing list says.
federation.sharing.configureRemote: Also turn on remote access (paired devices only) so other devices can reach this one
federation.sharing.confirm: Turn on library sharing? Devices you allow can browse everything in this device's library — view only, never change. No device is allowed automatically.
federation.sharing.confirmWithRemote: Turn on library sharing? Devices you allow can browse everything in this device's library — view only, never change. This also turns on remote access (paired devices only) so other devices can reach this one. No device is allowed automatically.
federation.sharing.stopConfirm: Turn off library sharing? Other devices can't browse this device until you turn it back on, and their searches and playback stop. The devices you allowed are kept and work again when sharing is back on. Who may manage this device doesn't change.
federation.sharing.codeTip: Single-use, expires soon. Enter it with this device's address on the device that should browse this library.
federation.sharing.codeExpired: This share code has expired. Create a new one when needed.
federation.sharing.remoteDisabled: Remote access is off, so other devices can't reach this device to browse it.
federation.pair.description: Enter its address. With a share code from it (created on it under Library sharing → Share this device's library), it's added at once; without one, a request is sent for its owner to allow. You can only browse it, never change anything there.
federation.pair.address: Address of the device to browse
federation.pair.shareBack: Also let it browse this device's library
federation.pair.shareBackTip: Turns on sharing here if it's off. Once the other device allows it, each can browse the other; with a share code it takes effect at once.
federation.pair.shareBackTipRemote: Turns on sharing here and remote access (paired devices only), so the other device can reach this one. Once it allows it, each can browse the other; with a share code it takes effect at once.
federation.pair.directionTip: Unticked, only this device can browse the other one; it can't browse this device.
federation.pair.awaitingApproval: Waiting for the other device to approve.
federation.pair.granted: Allowed: you can now browse its library.
federation.pair.rejected: The request to browse was rejected.
federation.requests.outgoingTitle: Requests to browse sent from this device
federation.requests.replacesExisting: A device claiming to be the same one can already browse this library; allowing this replaces its access. The name is the requester's own claim and isn't verified — make sure the address belongs to the device you expect.
federation.requests.offersReciprocal: Allowing this also lets this device browse {{name}}
federation.requests.approveConfirm: Let {{name}} browse this device's library? It can search, view and play everything here, but not change anything. This does not let this device browse {{name}}.
federation.requests.approveConfirmFrom: Let {{name}} at {{address}} browse this device's library? Make sure the address belongs to the device you expect. It can search, view and play everything here, but not change anything. This does not let this device browse {{name}}.
federation.requests.approveConfirmRecipr: Let {{name}} browse this device's library? It can search, view and play everything here, but not change anything. This device also gets to browse {{name}}.
federation.requests.approveConfirmFromRe: Let {{name}} at {{address}} browse this device's library? Make sure the address belongs to the device you expect. It can search, view and play everything here, but not change anything. This device also gets to browse {{name}}.
federation.mappings.title: Path mappings on this device
federation.mappings.tip: Where its shared folders are on this device. Used to play files and open their folders here; files are never moved or copied.
federation.discovery.noneFound: No nearby device is sharing. The other device has to turn on sharing under Library sharing → Share this device's library first; you can also enter its address above.
federation.error.network: The request could not be completed. Check this device and try again.
federation.error.QueryDeadlineExceeded: The query preparation deadline was exceeded. Try again when the device is available.
federation.error.ScanBudgetExceeded: Reading the library exceeded its scan budget. The device needs more capacity or a revised scan limit.
federation.error.ResultSnapshotTooLarge: The result snapshot is too large. Narrow the name or file filters and search again.
federation.error.Busy: This device is busy. Wait a moment and retry.
federation.error.QuerySessionExpired: The result session expired. Search again to continue.
federation.error.QuerySessionInterrupted: A participating device could not continue this page. Existing results are kept; retry the page or start a new search.
federation.error.CursorSuperseded: This page cursor is no longer available. Start a new search.
federation.error.LibraryEpochChanged: That device's library was restored from a backup or replaced. Search again; if you still can't browse it, add it again.
federation.error.ResourceGone: This resource is no longer available on its source device.
federation.error.AssetGone: This media asset is no longer available or its session expired. Open its details again.
federation.error.GrantRevoked: That device revoked this device's access to its library. Ask to browse it again to continue.
federation.error.InvalidNodeSignature: This device's access to it couldn't be verified. Add it again under Library sharing.
federation.error.SharingDisabled: That device has library sharing turned off.
federation.error.RemoteAccessDisabled: That device has remote access turned off, so no other device can reach it.
federation.error.UnsupportedQuery: A query field or value is not supported. Change the query; unsupported filters are never silently dropped.
federation.error.ProtocolIncompatible: That device runs an incompatible Bakabase version. Update both devices to the latest version.
federation.error.IdentityConflict: The device at this address isn't the one you added, or its library was restored from a backup. Check the address; if it's right, add the device again under Library sharing.
federation.error.InvalidCursor: This result cursor is invalid. Start a new search.
federation.error.RequestTooLarge: This request is too large. Select fewer items or devices.
federation.error.MalformedQuery: The query is invalid. Check its filters and selected devices.
federation.error.PlayerUnavailable: No supported local player could be opened. Use the browser preview or configure a local player.
federation.error.PlayerProxyUnsupported: The current player and proxy settings cannot guarantee a direct connection for this resource. Use the built-in preview, configure a local directory mapping, or install mpv (IINA is also available on macOS), then try again.
federation.error.MediaUnsupported: This browser cannot play the media format. Try a supported local player.
federation.identity.title: After copying or restoring data
federation.identity.tip: Only for the two cases below, and only on the computer they happened to. Disconnect this computer from the network first and reconnect when done. Your library data is never deleted. Just moving the data folder, without going back to older data, needs nothing here.
federation.identity.question: What happened?
federation.identity.copied.title: This computer's data was copied from another one
federation.identity.copied.removes: Clears: the devices that can manage this one (disconnected at once), the devices in library sharing and their path mappings, pending requests and share codes. The device name goes back to the computer's name; library sharing and the Multi-device library turn off.
federation.identity.copied.keeps: Keeps: your library data and the devices this one manages. The original computer, and the devices working with it, are not affected. Note: the devices it manages take this computer and the original for one; choosing Stop managing here also ends the original's management of that device.
federation.identity.copied.after: Afterwards: reconnect; turn sharing back on and add the devices you want to browse with; devices that should manage this computer must pair again.
federation.identity.restored.title: I restored this computer's data from a backup
federation.identity.restored.removes: Revokes: every device's access to this library, pending requests to browse it, and share codes. Library sharing and the Multi-device library turn off; devices browsing this one are told its library changed and must add it again.
federation.identity.restored.keeps: Keeps: the device name, the devices this one browses and their path mappings, who may manage this device, and the devices it manages.
federation.identity.restored.after: Afterwards: first check Management → Who may manage this device and revoke anything that shouldn't be there (the backup may have brought back devices you had removed); then reconnect, turn sharing on, and give share codes to, or allow requests from, the devices that should browse this one.
federation.identity.confirm: Make this computer a new device? Other devices will see it as a new device, no longer mixed up with the original. Devices that can manage it are removed and disconnected at once; devices in library sharing, path mappings, requests and share codes are cleared; the device name goes back to the computer's name; library sharing and the Multi-device library turn off. Library data and the devices this one manages are kept, and the original computer is not affected.
federation.recovery.title: Library sharing settings can't be read
federation.recovery.description: The file holding this device's library sharing settings can't be read, so it was left untouched rather than overwritten. If you have a backup of the Bakabase data folder, restore the file from it and choose Retry; otherwise, reset these settings.
federation.recovery.confirm: Reset library sharing settings? All devices in library sharing, their path mappings, pending requests and this device's name are cleared, and library sharing and the Multi-device library turn off. Other devices will see this one as a new device and must add it again. Your library data, the devices this one manages and who may manage it don't change.
federation.error.NodeUnreachable: Can't reach that device. Check its address, and that remote access is on there.
federation.error.NodeNotAuthorized: This device can't browse it right now. Ask to browse it again.
federation.error.ProtocolUnsupported: That device runs an incompatible Bakabase version. Update both devices to the latest version.
federation.error.PairingExpired: The request expired. Send a new one.
federation.error.PairingRejected: The other device rejected this request.
federation.error.PairingBusy: The other device is busy. Try again in a moment.
federation.error.PairingRateLimited: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
federation.error.InvalidAddress: Enter a valid HTTP or HTTPS device address.
federation.error.SelfAddress: That's this device's own address. Enter another device's address.
federation.error.SameIdentity: The device at this address identifies as this device. If the address leads back here (a reverse proxy, a port forward, your router's public address), use the other device's own address. Otherwise one of the two was copied from the other: on the copy, open Devices and sharing → Advanced → After copying or restoring data and choose Make this a new device (on a server without a window, such as Docker or a NAS, run dotnet Bakabase.Service.dll federation new-identity in it), then try again.
federation.error.PortMissing: Add the port to the address, as the other device shows it, for example 192.168.1.5:34567.
federation.error.InvalidNodeResponse: That device's answer couldn't be read. Make sure both devices run similar Bakabase versions.
federation.error.NodeSessionChanged: Access to that device just changed. Search again.
federation.error.NodeRedirectRefused: The device redirected this request. Check its configured address.
federation.error.MediaPlaybackFailed: The preview could not continue. Reopen the details to refresh access, check that the source device is online, or try a supported local player.
federation.browsing.title: Multi-device library
federation.browsing.description: When on, the Multi-device library searches this device together with the devices you can browse. It doesn't share this device's library with anyone.
federation.browsing.disableTip: Turning it off ends current searches and previews; added devices, path mappings and sharing settings are kept.
federation.directory.open: Open containing folder on this device
federation.directory.tip: Uses a file on this device or a directory mapping. The source device never opens a window.
federation.error.NoLinkedFile: This resource has no linked file or folder.
federation.error.PathMappingRequired: Configure a directory mapping for this device in Devices before opening this folder.
federation.error.MappedPathUnavailable: The mapped folder is unavailable on this device. Check the mapping and whether the drive is connected.
federation.error.OpenDirectoryUnavailabl: Opening folders is unavailable in this environment.
federation.error.BrowsingDisabled: The Multi-device library is off. Turn it on to search or preview.
federation.error.PathMappingsChanged: These mappings changed while you were editing. Refresh and review the current mappings before saving again.
federation.error.AssetExpired: Access to this media has expired. Close and reopen the resource details, then try again.
federation.error.MappingChanged: The directory mapping changed while this media was open. Start playback again.
federation.error.UnsupportedPlaybackMode: This media cannot be played that way. Use “Preview here” instead.
federation.error.InvalidPeerResponse: The other device returned an unexpected response. Make sure both devices run compatible Bakabase versions, then try again.
federation.error.InvalidPairingCode: The share code is wrong or has expired. Create a new one on the other device and try again.
federation.error.LocalInterfaceOnly: This page only works in Bakabase on this computer. Open it from the Bakabase window on the computer you want to manage.
federation.error.FederationEndpointDenie: This request was refused. Open this page from the Bakabase window on this device and try again; if it keeps happening, check the logs.
federation.error.InternalError: Bakabase on this device could not complete the request. Try again; if it keeps happening, check the Bakabase logs.
federation.error.SharingStateUnavailable: This device's library sharing settings can't be read. They weren't overwritten; restore them from a backup or reset them above.
federation.error.InvalidDeviceName: Use a device name of at most 64 characters without control characters.
federation.error.NoReachableAddress: This device has no network address the other device could reach, so it can't browse this one. Check the network, or untick “Also let it browse this device's library” and try again.
federation.mappings.conflictTip: These saved mappings would be changed or removed. Keep the current mappings or explicitly replace them with the changes shown below. New mappings are retained in either case.
federation.mappings.changedDuringReview: The saved mappings changed. Review the latest values below, then choose again to confirm.
federation.identity.restoreConfirm: Revoke every device's access to this library and turn off library sharing and the Multi-device library? The backup may have brought back devices you had revoked; this shuts them out too. Devices browsing this one stop and must add it again. The device name, the devices this one browses, path mappings and who may manage this device don't change.
federation.identity.restoreWarning: The backup also brings back the devices that could manage this one then, and this doesn't touch them. Check Who may manage this device afterwards.
federation.switcher.label: Switch device — showing {{name}}
federation.switcher.empty: No other devices yet. Add one under Devices and sharing → Management.
federation.switcher.openFailed: Could not switch to that device. Check that it is still managed from this device, then try again.
federation.switcher.listFailed: Could not load the devices this device manages.
federation.servers.title: Devices this device manages
federation.servers.empty: This device doesn't manage any other device yet. Add one below.
federation.servers.unrestricted: {{name}} lets any device on its network control it fully without pairing. To require pairing, open it, and on its {{page}} page set “{{setting}}” to “{{enabled}}”, then turn on “{{pairing}}”. This device never changes it for you.
federation.servers.revokedTip: {{name}} has revoked this device's access. Choose Stop managing, then add it again.
federation.servers.wrongServerTip: {{address}} is now another device ({{other}}), not {{name}}, so this device sends it nothing. If {{name}} moved, find it with “{{discover}}” below and add it again at its new address; its path mappings are kept. If {{name}} was reinstalled or its data was wiped, choose Stop managing and add it again.
federation.servers.wrongServerThisDevice: {{address}} now leads to this device itself, not {{name}}, so this device sends it nothing. If {{name}} moved, find it with “{{discover}}” below and add it again at its new address; its path mappings are kept.
federation.servers.wrongServerSameIdenti: {{address}} is now another computer ({{other}}) that identifies as this device — most likely its data was copied from here — not {{name}}, so this device sends it nothing. On the copy, open Devices and sharing → Advanced → After copying or restoring data and choose Make this a new device (on a server without a window, such as Docker or a NAS, run dotnet Bakabase.Service.dll federation new-identity in it). If {{name}} moved, find it with “{{discover}}” below and add it again at its new address; its path mappings are kept.
federation.servers.forgetConfirm: Stop managing {{name}}? This device asks {{name}} to revoke its access, then deletes the key and path mappings it keeps for it. Nothing else on {{name}} changes. Add it again to manage it later.
federation.servers.waiting: Waiting for someone on {{name}} to approve — expires in {{minutes}} min. This page updates by itself.
federation.servers.retrying: Could not get an answer from {{name}} on the last try. Still waiting for approval — this device keeps asking until the request expires in {{minutes}} min.
federation.servers.paired: {{name}} added. Choose Open in this window to manage it.
federation.servers.requested: Request sent. Allow it on {{name}} — a notification there leads to it.
federation.servers.approved: {{name}} agreed: you can manage it now.
federation.servers.requestClosed: The request to {{name}} is no longer pending — it was rejected or expired.
federation.servers.add.title: Add a device to manage
federation.servers.add.description: Enter its address. With a pairing code from it (created on it under Management → Who may manage this device), it's added at once; without one, a request goes to that device for someone there to allow.
federation.servers.add.address: Address of the device to manage
federation.servers.add.tip: Managing means full control: changing settings, deleting files, running tasks. Only want to browse its library? Use Library sharing instead.
federation.servers.add.noneFound: No other devices found nearby. You can still enter an address.
federation.servers.mappings.title: Path mappings on this device
federation.servers.mappings.tip: Where its library folders are on this device. Needed to play its files or open their folders here.
federation.error.ManagedServerAwaitingAp: Waiting for the other device to approve.
federation.error.ManagedServerUnreachabl: Nothing answered at that address. Check the address, and that Bakabase is running on that device with remote access on.
federation.error.ManagedServerNotBakabas: Something answered at that address, but it is not Bakabase.
federation.error.ManagedServerThisAppToo: That device runs a newer Bakabase. Update this app first.
federation.error.ManagedServerServerTooO: Bakabase on that device is too old to be managed from here. Update it first.
federation.error.ManagedServerRemoteAcce: Remote access is off on that device, so it can't be managed. Turn it on there under Devices and sharing → Management → Who may manage this device.
federation.error.ManagedServerThisDevice: That address is this device. Enter another device's address.
federation.error.ManagedServerCodeReject: The pairing code is wrong or has expired. Create a new code on the other device.
federation.error.ManagedServerRequestRej: The request was rejected, or expired before anyone answered.
federation.error.ManagedServerTooManyAtt: That device is refusing more attempts from here for now. Wait a few minutes and try again.
federation.error.ManagedServerPairingUns: That device cannot pair: its Bakabase is too old, or pairing is turned off there.
federation.error.ManagedServerInvalidAdd: That is not a device address. Enter its host and port, for example 192.168.1.5:34567.
federation.error.ManagedServerPortMissin: Add the port to the address, as the other device shows it, for example 192.168.1.5:34567.
federation.error.ManagedServerSameIdenti: The device at that address identifies as this device — was one of them copied from the other? On the copy, open Devices and sharing → Advanced → After copying or restoring data and choose Make this a new device (on a server without a window, run dotnet Bakabase.Service.dll federation new-identity), then try again.
federation.error.ManagementUnavailable: This device can't manage other devices — only the desktop app on a computer can.
federation.error.ServerNotManaged: This device no longer manages that device. Refresh the list.
federation.error.UnknownServer: This device no longer manages that device. Switch back to this device and refresh its list.
federation.error.RelayUnavailable: This device could not open a local port to show that device. Try again in a moment; if it keeps failing, restart Bakabase.
federation.error.InvalidRequest: This device could not read that request. Reload the page and try again.
federation.error.UnsupportedMediaType: This device did not accept the format of that request. Reload the page and try again.
federation.management.title: Who may manage {{target}}
federation.management.description: A paired device — a computer or a phone — gets full control of {{target}}: settings, files and tasks. Give it a pairing code, or allow its request.
federation.management.status.unrestricte: Unrestricted · any device has full control
federation.management.loadFailed: Could not read who may manage {{target}}.
federation.management.failed: The change could not be made. Try again.
federation.management.offTip: Remote access is off: no other device can reach {{target}}, so none can manage it or browse its library.
federation.management.enable: Turn on remote access for {{target}} (paired devices only)
federation.management.enableConfirm: Turn on remote access for {{target}}, for paired devices only? Other devices can then pair with a code from here or send a request for you to allow. A paired device gets full control; a device that isn't paired can't reach it.
federation.management.unrestricted: Any device on the same network can control {{target}} fully without pairing — change settings, delete files, start programs.
federation.management.unpairedBrowse: Devices that aren't paired can still open {{target}} in a browser to view and play — whatever the library sharing list says. Only paired devices can manage it.
federation.management.requirePairingConf: Allow only paired devices to reach {{target}}? Paired devices keep working; a device that isn't paired loses access at once and has to pair first.
Change {{target}} from Unrestricted to paired devices only? Paired devices keep working; any other device or browser loses access at once and has to pair first.
federation.management.lockOutWarning: This browser isn't paired, so it loses access too. If you still need this window, make the change from a paired device or from the device itself.
federation.management.code.tip: Single-use, expires soon. Enter it with the address on the other device, and that device gets full control of {{target}}.
federation.management.requests.title: Asking to manage {{target}}
federation.management.requests.approveCo: Let {{name}} manage {{target}}? It gets full control: settings, files and tasks.
Let {{name}} at {{address}} manage {{target}}? It gets full control: settings, files and tasks. Make sure the address belongs to the device you expect.
federation.management.devices.title: Devices that can manage {{target}}
federation.management.devices.revokeConf: Revoke {{name}}'s access to manage {{target}}? It is disconnected at once and has to pair again to get back in.
federation.management.devices.revokeSelf: This is the device you're using. Revoking it ends this window's access to {{target}}; you'll have to pair again to manage it.
federation.console.localOnly: This window is showing a device you manage. The Multi-device pages belong to this device's own view.
federation.map.title: Device map
federation.map.intro: This device in the middle, your other Bakabase devices around it, and a line for every connection between them: who can browse whose library, and who manages whom. Select a device or a line to see its details and act on it.
federation.map.large.note: {{count}} devices are more than a map this wide can draw readably, so each is listed here with its connections. Select a device or a connection for its details and actions; a wider window shows them as a map.
federation.map.issue.wrongServer: Another server answers at its address
federation.map.issue.unrestricted: Anyone on its network can manage it
federation.map.issue.requestEnded: The request to manage it has ended
federation.map.edge.label: {{kind}} with {{name}}: {{summary}}
federation.map.direction.sharing.in.pend: Waiting for approval to browse {{name}}'s library
federation.map.direction.sharing.out.pen: {{name}} asks to browse this device's library
federation.map.attention.sharing.in: This device cannot browse {{name}}'s library right now: {{issue}}
federation.map.attention.management.out: This device cannot manage {{name}} right now: {{issue}}
federation.map.node.label: {{name}}: {{summary}}
federation.map.hint: Select a device or a line on the map to see its details and what you can do.
federation.map.legend.title: Legend
federation.map.legend.sharing: Library sharing — points to the device that may browse
federation.map.legend.management: Management — points from the manager to the managed device
federation.map.legend.attention: Dotted, with a warning mark: set up, but not working right now
federation.map.legend.unverified: Known only from its own request — not verified
federation.map.list.title: Devices and connections
federation.map.source.sharing: Library sharing could not be read, so its connections are missing from the map.
federation.map.source.servers: The devices this device manages could not be read, so they are missing from the map.
federation.map.source.access: The devices that may manage this one could not be read, so they are missing from the map.
federation.map.discovery.none: No other devices found nearby. You can still add one by its address on the Devices and sharing page.
federation.map.empty.title: Only this device so far
federation.map.empty.body: Multi-device connects the Bakabase servers on your network — the desktop app on each computer, and servers on a NAS or in Docker. Connect a device and this map shows who can browse whose library and who manages whom.
federation.map.panel.unverified: Its name and identity come from its own request and are not verified. Check the address before approving.
federation.map.panel.claim.knownAt: It says it is {{name}}, which this device knows at {{known}}. This request came from {{from}}.
federation.map.panel.claim.known: It says it is {{name}}, a device this one already knows. This request came from {{from}}.
federation.map.panel.claim.unknownFrom: an address it did not give
federation.map.panel.shareMine.title: Let {{name}} browse this device's library
federation.map.panel.shareMine.tip: Create a share code here, then on {{name}} enter this device's address and the code under Library sharing → Add a device to browse.
federation.map.panel.shareMine.enableFir: Turn on sharing under Devices and sharing → Library sharing first
federation.map.panel.management.none: Neither this device nor {{name}} manages the other.
federation.map.panel.matchedByName: Shown here because the device paired to manage this one uses the same name, “{{name}}”.
federation.map.panel.namesakes.one: May be the same device as another device of the same name. Nothing else shows they are one device, so they are shown apart:
federation.map.panel.namesakes.many: May be the same device as one of {{count}} other devices of the same name. Nothing else shows it is any of them, so each is shown apart:
federation.map.namesake.role.manager: the device that manages this one
federation.map.namesake.role.sharesWithT: the device sharing its library with this one
federation.map.namesake.role.browsesThis: the device browsing this device's library
federation.map.namesake.role.sharing: the device paired for library sharing
federation.map.namesake.role.askedToMana: the device this one asked to manage
federation.map.namesake.role.askedToBrow: the device whose library this one asked to browse
federation.map.panel.manageTip: This gives this device full control of {{name}}. It's separate from library sharing and uses its own pairing codes, created on {{name}} under Management → Who may manage this device.
federation.map.panel.moved.title: Manage {{name}} at {{address}}
federation.map.panel.moved.tip: {{name}} answers as itself at {{address}}. Pairing with it again there keeps its path mappings and its window on this computer.
federation.map.panel.moved.checking: Looking for {{name}} where it was last seen…
federation.map.panel.moved.gone: {{address}} no longer answers as {{name}}, so nothing was sent there. Look for it again with “Find nearby devices”.
federation.map.panel.wrongServerTip: {{address}} now answers as another server ({{other}}), not {{name}}, so this computer sends it nothing. If {{name}} moved to another address, “{{discover}}” at the top of the map finds where it is now, and this panel then offers to pair with it there — its path mappings are kept. If it was reinstalled or its data was reset, it is a new install: stop managing this entry and pair with it again.
federation.map.panel.wrongServerThisDevi: {{address}} now reaches this computer itself, not {{name}}, so this computer sends it nothing. If {{name}} moved to another address, “{{discover}}” at the top of the map finds where it is now, and this panel then offers to pair with it there — its path mappings are kept.
federation.map.panel.wrongServerSameIden: {{address}} is now another computer ({{other}}) that identifies as this device — most likely its data was copied from here — not {{name}}, so this device sends it nothing. On the copy, open Devices and sharing → Advanced → After copying or restoring data and choose Make this a new device (on a server without a window, such as Docker or a NAS, run dotnet Bakabase.Service.dll federation new-identity in it). If {{name}} moved, “{{discover}}” at the top of the map finds where it is now, and this panel then offers to pair with it there; its path mappings are kept.
federation.map.panel.self.managedBy: Devices that can manage this one
federation.map.panel.ghost.sharing: It shares its library on this network: you can ask to browse it.
federation.map.panel.ghost.management: It answers management discovery: you can ask to manage it.
federation.map.panel.ghost.nothing: This window cannot connect to it. Use the Devices and sharing page in the desktop app on a computer.
